name: Synthetic ghost: Thomas pattern right, then burst both sides (Persinger 2000)
origin: Persinger, Tiller & Koren (Laurentian University), 2000 case study of one man who had experienced a haunt
summary: Persinger's lab tried to re-create one man's earlier 'haunt': a frequency-modulated (Thomas) pattern over the right hemisphere, then a second pattern through both hemispheres. The lab reported rushes of fear and an apparition during the right-sided pattern and pleasant experiences during the bilateral one, in one unblinded subject.
notes: Persinger, Tiller & Koren (2000) exposed one 45-year-old man to 1 uT complex transcerebral fields: a frequency-modulated pattern over the right hemisphere, then a second pattern applied bilaterally. The lab reported that within 10 min of the right-sided pattern he felt 'rushes of fear' that ended in an apparition he judged very similar to his natural one, with 1-2 s paroxysmal 15 Hz complex spikes in the EEG, and that the bilateral pattern brought pleasant experiences. The paper gives no exposure durations ('within 10 min' is an onset latency); 30 + 30 min follows the lab's own two-phase sensed-presence protocol (30 min of the frequency-modulated pattern, then 30 min of BurstX; Saroka 2015) and its stated 20-40 min per pattern. The frequency-modulated pattern is taken to be the Thomas pattern (Saroka equates the two) and plays the exact patent table, 849 points at 3 ms (Buckner 2015), with a 3-ms pause between repeats: the point and interstimulus durations at which this pattern provoked the most seizures in the lab's epileptic rats (Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999). The second pattern is not named; the lab's burst-firing pattern stands in for it (an inference from Saroka's protocol). Its point values are unpublished, so an accelerating burst of 230 points at 3 ms (690 ms) once every 4 s (Martin & Persinger 2004; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009 give about 0.7 s every 3 s) approximates it. Two static coils per side, T8/TP8 and T7/TP7, approximate 'over the right hemisphere' and 'bilaterally'. Unlike this file, persinger-saroka-2015-sensed-presence plays the Thomas phase on both sides, as Saroka describes, and god-helmet-classic is Murphy's Shiva version (a chirp approximation and a burst stepping around four coils per side). French et al. (2009) based the waveform of their room-scale Haunt study on this paper's; with 79 people the reports were unrelated to condition and best explained by suggestibility. This is n = 1, unblinded, in a man chosen because he had had the experience and who knew the purpose: a case report, not evidence of an effect. Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Phase 1 is the part the lab reported as frightening: press Skip to go to phase 2, and stop at once on fear or distress. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; not for anyone with anxiety or trauma symptoms; have someone nearby.
setting: Seated in a quiet, dark room with the eyes covered (the lab used blindfolds or opaque goggles in an acoustic chamber); the original subject had EEG recorded throughout.
schedule: One session in the original. At most weekly; for a self-test, use the app's Blind option and write down what you felt before unblinding.
